definitions.explanation: winning a match without playing because the opponent forfeits, withdraws, or fails to appear

examples.japanese: ⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{棄権|きけん}→棄権：16194_kiken⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{不戦勝|ふせんしょう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: We won by default due to the opponent's withdrawal.

examples.japanese: {不戦勝|ふせんしょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ラウンド→ラウンド：24227_raundo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{進|すす}んだ→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: We advanced to the next round with a walkover.

examples.japanese: {怪我|けが}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出場|しゅつじょう}→出場：03223_shutsujou⟧⟦でき→できる：00557_dekiru⟧ず、⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{不戦勝|ふせんしょう}になった。
examples.english: Unable to compete due to injury, the opposing team won by default.

notes:
FORMS:
{不|ふ} (not) + ⟦{戦|せん}→〜戦：28346_sen⟧ (fight, battle) + {勝|しょう} (victory) → victory without fighting

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{不戦敗|ふせんぱい}→不戦敗：22302_fusenpai⟧ (loss by default, forfeit)

USAGE:
Common in sports tournaments and sumo wrestling when an opponent cannot compete due to injury, illness, or other reasons.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{棄権|きけん}→棄権：16194_kiken⟧ (withdrawal, forfeit)
- ⟦{欠場|けつじょう}→欠場：18521_ketsujou⟧ (absence from a match)
- ⟦{失格|しっかく}→失格：12195_shikkaku⟧ (disqualification)
